words.sense: In perfect original condition, clean and unspoiled.
misconceptions: Assuming old objects cannot be spotlessly clean.
Ignoring changes to original material or condition.

words.sense: Spotlessly clean, though it may be old or frequently used.
misconceptions: Ignoring changes to original material or condition.

semantic_axes.description: Pristine emphasizes original, unspoiled condition; immaculate emphasizes spotless cleanliness regardless of age or use.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Farah’s rare paperback?

beats.text: Farah found a forty-year-old book still sealed in its original wrapper, without a bent page.
beats.reason: Original wrapper and unworn pages. Original condition without wear.

beats.text: Its cover design was out of fashion, but the book had never been opened.
beats.decisive_clue: outdated style does not spoil original condition
beats.reason: Outdated style does not spoil original condition. Original condition without wear.

chains.feedback_short: Outdated style does not spoil original condition makes pristine the better fit.
chains.feedback_deep: Pristine means in perfect original condition, clean and unspoiled; immaculate means spotlessly clean, though it may be old or frequently used. Here, outdated style does not spoil original condition; that is why pristine wins even after the new detail.
chains.contrast_rule: Pristine is unspoiled; immaculate is spotless.
